title: Elisha's Miracles
hint: The prophet with a double portion (2 Kings 2-6)
intro: Elisha asked for a double share of Elijah's spirit—and received it. The Bible records at least 14 miracles performed by Elisha, twice as many as those of Elijah. Here is the overview from 2 Kings 2-6.

items.title: Parting the Jordan River
items.text: Elisha struck the water with Elijah's cloak, and the water parted. He crossed over on dry ground. (2:14)

items.title: Purifying the Water at Jericho
items.text: The water at Jericho was bad and the land unfruitful. Elisha threw salt into the spring and healed the water. (2:19-22)

items.title: The Bears and the Youths
items.text: Youths mocked Elisha: "Go up, you baldhead!" He cursed them, and two bears came out and tore forty-two of them apart. (2:23-24)

items.title: Oil for the Widow
items.text: A prophet's widow had only a jar of oil. Elisha told her to gather empty jars. The oil flowed until all the jars were full. (4:1-7)

items.title: The Shunammite Woman Bears a Son
items.text: The wealthy woman from Shunem was childless. Elisha promised her a son, and she gave birth within a year. (4:8-17)

items.title: The Boy Raised to Life
items.text: The boy died. Elisha lay on him, and the boy came back to life—he sneezed seven times. (4:18-37)

items.title: The Poisonous Stew Healed
items.text: The prophets were cooking stew with poisonous gourds. "There is death in the pot!" Elisha threw flour into it, and the food became safe to eat. (4:38-41)

items.title: Feeding a Hundred Men
items.text: With twenty loaves of barley bread, Elisha fed a hundred men, and there was some left over—as the Lord had said. (4:42-44)

items.title: Naaman Healed
items.text: The Syrian commander was healed of leprosy by dipping himself seven times in the Jordan. (5:1-14)

items.title: The Iron Axe Head Floats
items.text: An axe head fell into the river. Elisha threw a stick into the water, and the iron floated to the surface. (6:1-7)

footer.title: Elisha and Jesus
footer.content: Several of Elisha's miracles point forward to Jesus: raising the dead, feeding many with little bread, and healing lepers. Jesus himself mentioned Elisha and Naaman as examples (Luke 4:27).
